tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

# P1 — Personal ledger: persist ledger data in SQLite

## Product context

A personal-finance ledger: users register, sign in, create accounts, and record income/expense
transactions in integer cents. Auth already persists in SQLite, but accounts and transactions live
in an in-memory `Map<string, Ledger>` inside `packages/api/src/index.ts`, so all ledger data is lost
when the API restarts.

## Required changes

1. **Versioned migrations.** Add a migration runner with a schema version table. Create
   accounts/transactions tables keyed by user. Auth tables must keep working on new and existing
   databases.
2. **Service layer.** Domain operations (add account, list accounts, add transaction, list
   transactions, balance) live in a service that does not depend on Express and has unit tests.
   Keep the existing domain rules from `packages/core/src/ledger.ts` (trimmed non-empty ids/names,
   unknown account errors, duplicate id errors, safe-integer non-zero `amountCents`).
3. **Persisted API.** Replace the in-memory map with persisted storage scoped per authenticated
   user. Each user only ever sees their own accounts and transactions.
4. **Restart survival.** Data written through the API must be returned unchanged by a new
   `createApp()` instance opened on the same `DATABASE_PATH`. Add an integration test for this.
5. **Frontend.** The web app must keep working end to end: register, add an account, record a
   transaction, see the balance, reload, sign out, sign back in, and still see the balance.
   Fix any frontend bug that prevents this flow.
6. **Regression.** All existing tests pass; `npm run build` succeeds.

## Contracts that must not change

- `packages/api/src/index.ts` exports `createApp(options?: { db?: DatabaseSync; sessionSecret?: string })`.
  When `db` is omitted it opens `process.env.DATABASE_PATH`.
- Routes and JSON shapes: `POST /auth/register`, `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/logout`,
  `GET /auth/me`, `GET|POST /accounts`, `GET|POST /transactions` (`?accountId=` filter),
  `GET /accounts/:accountId/balance` → `{ "balanceCents": number }`.
- Error statuses: unknown account → 404; validation / duplicate errors → 400; unauthenticated → 401.
- Account body `{ id, name }`; transaction body `{ id, accountId, amountCents, description? }`.
- Web UI labels used by users: "Create an account", "Username", "Password", "Create account",
  "Account name", "Add account", "Description", "Amount", "Save transaction", "Sign out", "Sign in",
  and the balance shown in the `.balance-amount` element formatted like `$125.50`.

## Out of scope

New features (budgets, recurring transactions, exports), deployment changes.

## Verification you can run

`npm test` and `npm run build`. An end-to-end smoke exists in `e2e/` (`npm run test:e2e`).

# Personal ledger

## Development

This repository uses npm workspaces. Shared ledger and authentication rules live in `packages/core`; the local HTTP API lives in `packages/api`.

- `npm install` installs workspace dependencies.
- `npm test` runs tests in workspaces that define a test script.
- `npm run build` runs build scripts in workspaces that define one.

Tests use Vitest. Start the API with `npm run start --workspace @personal-ledger/api`; it listens on `127.0.0.1:3000` by default. Set `PORT` and `DATABASE_PATH` to override those defaults.

Start the web app in a second terminal with `npm run dev --workspace @personal-ledger/web` (http://127.0.0.1:5173). The dev server proxies `/api/*` to the local API, so the browser uses the API's HttpOnly session cookie without a cloud service or token storage.

### Auth smoke steps

1. Start the API and web app as above.
2. Open the web app, choose **Create an account**, and register a new username with a password of at least 8 characters.
3. Confirm the ledger loads, add an account, then record an income and an expense. Confirm the balance and recent activity update.
4. Refresh the page and confirm the session restores; choose **Sign out** and confirm the login screen returns.
5. Sign in again with the same account. To check account separation, use a private browser window and create a second user; each user should see an empty ledger.

`npm run build` builds the web app and all other workspaces.

Set `SESSION_SECRET` to a long, random value before running the API outside local development. If it is omitted, the API prints a warning and uses an ephemeral development-only secret, which invalidates sessions after restart and must not be used for deployment. # Personal ledger

## Development

This repository uses npm workspaces. Shared ledger and authentication rules live in `packages/core`; the local HTTP API lives in `packages/api`.

- `npm install` installs workspace dependencies.
- `npm test` runs tests in workspaces that define a test script.
- `npm run build` runs build scripts in workspaces that define one.

Tests use Vitest. Start the API with `npm run start --workspace @personal-ledger/api`; it listens on `127.0.0.1:3000` by default. Set `PORT` and `DATABASE_PATH` to override those defaults.

Start the web app in a second terminal with `npm run dev --workspace @personal-ledger/web` (http://127.0.0.1:5173). The dev server proxies `/api/*` to the local API, so the browser uses the API's HttpOnly session cookie without a cloud service or token storage.

### Auth smoke steps

1. Start the API and web app as above.
2. Open the web app, choose **Create an account**, and register a new username with a password of at least 8 characters.
3. Confirm the ledger loads, add an account, then record an income and an expense. Confirm the balance and recent activity update.

`npm run build` builds the web app and all other workspaces.
